correctness.rationale: Substituting \(g_t=\lambda x_t\) and \(\beta_1=\beta_2=0\) into Algorithm 1 gives exactly \(x_{t+1}=x_t(1-q_t)\) with \(q_t=a/M_t^{2p}\). If \(q_t\le2\), the historical maximum freezes and the dynamics become linear; if \(q_t>2\), a new maximum is created and \(q_{t+1}=q_t/(q_t-1)^{2p}\). For \(p\le1/4\), \((q-1)^{2p}\le\sqrt{q-1}\) and \(q>2\sqrt{q-1}\), so the interval \((2,\infty)\) is invariant and the decreasing sequence tends to its only fixed point \(2\). For \(p>1/4\), the derivative at the fixed point is \(1-4p<0\), so a decreasing orbit approaching from above must enter a neighborhood mapped below \(2\), giving finite stabilization. Fresh map iterations reproduced both regimes, and the frozen direct-Padam verifier was read.
correctness.risk: The conclusion is deliberately restricted to zero momentum, zero second-moment smoothing, fixed step, no denominator epsilon, and one dimension.

originality.rationale: Chen et al. define the exact max-memory Padam rule and their published theory also singles out \(p\le1/4\) in a stochastic convergence corollary, but that is a different theorem under different assumptions. In particular, their Theorem 4.3 requires \(\beta_1<\beta_2^{2p}\), which the boundary choice \(\beta_1=\beta_2=0\) does not satisfy. The paper does not derive the scalar overshoot map, the critical radius, persistent two-cycle, finite-crossing dichotomy, or exact resonance set. The follow-up convergence paper treats broad adaptive methods rather than this max-memory dynamical normal form. Resultary returned no matching phase-transition theorem.

final_claim: For the scalar quadratic and the exact fixed-step Padam boundary specialization \(\beta_1=\beta_2=0\), the max-memory dynamics have a sharp exponent transition at \(p=1/4\): for \(0<p\le1/4\) every sufficiently small nonzero initialization approaches the nonzero symmetric two-cycle at the critical radius, whereas for \(p>1/4\) overshoot crosses the stability threshold in finitely many steps and then converges geometrically, except for exact resonance at the two-cycle.
limitations: Fixed learning rate, \(\beta_1=\beta_2=0\), and no denominator epsilon.
